question: What does Cal Newport mean by 'deep work', and what is its opposite?
answer: Work done in distraction-free concentration that pushes your thinking to its limit, creating new value and improving skill. Its opposite is shallow work: email, meetings and admin, which are easy to copy. Newport argues that deep work is growing both rarer and more valuable, so those who cultivate it will thrive.
move: Hard, focused work is rare, which makes it valuable.
simply: Deep work is concentrating hard on one difficult thing, with no interruptions. Answering email is the opposite.
why: Most jobs fill up with shallow tasks by default. Protecting even an hour a day for deep work is often the biggest lever on what you produce.
